text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for people who did not write it. One key habit is following naming conventions, such as using clear and meaningful names for variables and functions. Another important idea is keeping functions small, so each one does only one job. This makes the code much easier to test and fix. When code is clean, it is also easier to maintain over time. Other developers can quickly find problems and add new features without breaking anything. In short, clean code saves time and reduces stress for everyone on the team.
